Followed Google Maps like a loyal adventurer, hoping to stumble upon the famous Batu Marhosa—the mysterious stone said to whistle when the wind hits just right. The location pinned? Yes, we arrived. The vibe? A little more “Where’s the batu?” than “marhosa!” To be fair, nature was doing its thing—there were signs of recent changes in the area: uprooted trees, shifts in vegetation, and an overall feeling that the landscape had been rearranged by something (weather? time? overzealous goats?). There was a small stream trickling through, sort of a waterfall if you squint, just like a fellow review had described. Peaceful? Yes. Whistling rocks? Not so much. We poked around a bit, hoping to hear the wind sing through a stone, but it didn’t feel like the kind of place you’d want to start ripping off leaves. More like a spot you pause, take a breath, and then quietly ask Google if maybe the pin’s a little off. So is it the real Batu Marhosa site? Could be. Is it worth the detour? Only if you’re already in Pangururan and feeling curious, cautious, and equipped with a local guided guide. Batu Marhosa might not have whistled for us, but the adventure lives on—just a little further up the trail. Note: If you’re feeling brave, stubborn, and have a heart of steel (and a sturdy bike)—you could venture even further up to Danau Aek Natonang. It’s a crater lake that takes some effort and determination to reach, especially on two wheels. Think gravel, slopes, landslides and a workout for your soul. It’d easily earn you a badge of Samosir explorer pride, and a slice of unknown peace but also magically transported into a near no-mans world that only the locals know

Salah satu tempat wisata yang sangat saya rekomendasikan. Lokasinya hanya berjarak sekitar 6 km dari jalan utama kota Balige. Sekitar 25 menit perjalanan. Pemandangan alam menuju ke sana juga indah sekali. Bukit-bukit yang hijau, dan saat melihat ke arah danau Toba, wuih, indahnya minta ampun. Jalanan ke sana termasuk bagus, kecuali sekitar 200 meter, persis sebelum anak tangga. Jalanan rusak cukup parah. Semoga pemerintah setempat memperhatikan hal ini. Untuk menuju ke air terjun, kita mesti menaiki sekitar 207 anak tangga, yang rata-rata tingginya 15 cm. Agak capek sih, namun rasa capek itu teayar dengan keindahan air terjun yang buagus sekali.... Segar sekali, karena di sini kita bisa mendapatkan banyak ion-ion negatif (yang amat sangat berguna bagi kesehatan). Kalo ke Balige, pastikan ke Air Terjun Siboruon ini.
